cancer_indication: PD-L1–positive unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) in combination with nab-paclitaxel (IMpassion130; indication withdrawn in the US in 2021).
moa: Atezolizumab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that blocks PD-L1 (CD274) on tumor and immune cells, preventing PD-L1 from engaging PD-1 on T cells. In breast cancer, its activity is most established in immunogenic TNBC where PD-L1 expression and tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes are present, enabling reactivation of anti-tumor T-cell function. The drug does not directly kill tumor cells; tumor control occurs via restored immune recognition and killing in tumors with a pre-existing but restrained anti-tumor immune response.

HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.description: Interferon-γ–driven immune activation program that includes interferon-responsive genes involved in antigen presentation and immune chemokine signaling.
HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.interpretation: This pathway reflects an immune-inflamed tumor microenvironment in breast cancer, supporting antigen presentation and immune-cell recruitment that underpins response to PD-L1 blockade.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: A high IFN-γ/T cell–inflamed signature (CXCL9/10, IDO1, HLA genes; MSigDB HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE) reflects pre-existing cytotoxic TILs and antigen presentation, which in TNBC is associated with better response to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade including atezolizumab.

Ayers et al., “IFN-γ–related mRNA profile predicts clinical response to PD-1 blockade.” J Clin Invest 2017;127:2930–2940. PMID: 28650338.(PubMed) Keenan et al., genomic correlates of response to ICIs in breast cancer. Nat Med 2019. PMID: 31308507.(Europe PMC) MSigDB HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE (M5913).(GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: IFN-γ–high tumors can still be resistant if chronic IFN-γ drives compensatory upregulation of multiple checkpoints (PD-L1, IDO1, LAG3, TIGIT) and T cell exhaustion, a failure pattern described across ICI-treated cancers and occasionally seen in breast cancer.

Benci et al., “Opposing Functions of Interferon Coordinate Adaptive and Innate Immune Responses to Cancer Immune Checkpoint Blockade.” Cell 2019. PMID: 30683432.(Cell) Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338.(PubMed)
Mechanistically accurate: IFN-γ–low (“non–T-cell-inflamed”) TNBC lacks primed CD8⁺ T cells and chemokines, predicting primary resistance to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors despite PD-L1 testing.
Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338.(PubMed) Keenan et al. Nat Med 2019, breast ICI correlates.(Europe PMC)
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: In breast cancer, robust benefit from atezolizumab without pre-existing IFN-γ/T cell–inflamed features is exceedingly unlikely, as cold tumors rarely convert to responders with PD-L1 monotherapy or atezolizumab–chemotherapy alone.
Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338.(PubMed) Han et al., “PD-1/PD-L1 pathway: current researches in cancer.” Cancer Treat Rev 2020. PMID: 32004790.

Mechanistically accurate: Effective PD-L1 blockade reinvigorates tumor-resident T cells, increasing IFN-γ production and expanding the IFN-γ gene signature alongside responses in TNBC (e.g., PD-L1⁺ cohorts in IMpassion130).

Schmid et al., “Atezolizumab and nab-paclitaxel in advanced TNBC.” N Engl J Med 2018;379:2108–2121. PMID: 30345906, NCT02425891.(New England Journal of Medicine) Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338.(PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some tumors show on-treatment IFN-γ/immune activation but still progress due to adaptive upregulation of alternate checkpoints or myeloid suppressive programs, a pattern reported in melanoma and likely relevant to a subset of TNBC.
Benci et al. Cell 2019, PMID: 30683432 (adaptive IFN-γ–driven resistance; cross-cancer extrapolation).(Cell)

Mechanistically accurate: Persistently low or further decreased IFN-γ signature after atezolizumab indicates failure to recruit/activate T cells, corresponding to primary or early acquired resistance in TNBC.
Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338.(PubMed) Keenan et al. Nat Med 2019, PMID: 31308507.(Europe PMC)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In responders, IFN-γ metrics may fall at late timepoints after substantial tumor clearance because antigen load and TCR stimulation drop, even though earlier IFN-γ induction was required for atezolizumab sensitivity.

Tumeh et al., “PD-1 blockade induces responses by inhibiting adaptive immune resistance.” Nature 2014. PMID: 24619099 (dynamic CD8/IFN-γ changes; cross-cancer).(Portland Press) Schmid et al. NEJM 2018, PMID: 30345906.(PubMed)

HALLMARK_ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION.description: Immune cytotoxicity and lymphocyte activation signature enriched for T-cell and NK-cell effector programs.
HALLMARK_ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION.interpretation: In breast tumors, this signature captures the presence and activity of cytotoxic immune infiltrates that are central to checkpoint inhibitor efficacy.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: The HALLMARK_ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION gene set captures a broad T cell–inflamed transcriptional program (Th1 cytokines, cytotoxic genes) that overlaps with IFN-γ/TIS signatures predicting PD-1/PD-L1 benefit, including in TNBC.
MSigDB HALLMARK_ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION (C2, Mxxxx).(GSEA MSigDB) Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338.(PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Strong allo-like immune activation with concurrent dominant suppressive mechanisms (Tregs, MDSCs, multiple checkpoints) may yield a transcriptionally “hot” yet functionally ineffective immune infiltrate.
Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338.(PubMed)

Mechanistically accurate: Low allograft-rejection signature reflects lack of effector T-cell recruitment and inflammatory chemokines, typical of immunologically cold breast tumors that fare poorly with PD-L1 blockade.
Han et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790. Keenan et al. Nat Med 2019.(Europe PMC)
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: In the absence of any T cell/allograft-rejection–like transcriptional activity, atezolizumab lacks effector cells to unleash, making true sensitivity highly implausible in breast cancer.
Keenan et al. Nat Med 2019 (T cell–inflamed vs non-inflamed ICIs).(Europe PMC)

Mechanistically accurate: Clinical responders to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade show expansion and activation of effector T cell/allograft-rejection–like programs on treatment, consistent with atezolizumab-induced immune activation.
Tumeh et al. Nature 2014. PMID: 24619099.(Portland Press) Schmid et al. NEJM 2018, PMID: 30345906.(PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: A paradoxical scenario where transcriptomics show allo-rejection–like activation but radiologic progression suggests either immune-excluded niches or compensatory immune escape.
Benci et al. Cell 2019, PMID: 30683432 (adaptive resistance; cross-cancer).(Cell)
Mechanistically accurate: Lack of increase or loss of allo-rejection/T cell–inflamed genes under atezolizumab indicates absent or exhausted T-cell engagement and correlates with non-response.
Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338.(PubMed)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: After initial tumor control and immune activation, late samples from responders may show contraction of allo-rejection gene expression as antigen burden decreases.
Tumeh et al. Nature 2014. PMID: 24619099 (dynamic immune changes; cross-cancer).(Portland Press)

WP_CANCER_IMMUNOTHERAPY_BY_PD1_BLOCKADE.description: Checkpoint signaling pathway describing PD-1/PD-L1–mediated inhibition of T-cell activation and its therapeutic blockade.
WP_CANCER_IMMUNOTHERAPY_BY_PD1_BLOCKADE.interpretation: This pathway is the core axis targeted by atezolizumab (via PD-L1), and its activity defines immune suppression that can be released by PD-L1 blockade in breast cancer.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High expression of genes in WP_CANCER_IMMUNOTHERAPY_BY_PD1_BLOCKADE (WP4585; MSigDB M39843) reflects engaged PD-1 axis and activated T cells, a prerequisite for benefit from PD-L1 blockade in TNBC.
MSigDB WP_CANCER_IMMUNOTHERAPY_BY_PD1_BLOCKADE (C2:CP:WIKIPATHWAYS).(New England Journal of Medicine) Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Highly engaged PD-1/PD-L1 signaling can still coexist with intrinsic tumor escape mechanisms (e.g., β-catenin or PTEN loss) that blunt response despite pathway engagement.
Spranger et al., β-catenin–driven immune exclusion (melanoma; cross-cancer).(GSEA MSigDB) Keenan et al. Nat Med 2019.(Europe PMC)
Mechanistically accurate: Low PD-1-axis pathway engagement implies minimal PD-L1/PD-1 interaction at baseline, limiting the therapeutic target for atezolizumab in breast tumors.
Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790.
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Without PD-1-axis activation, blocking PD-L1 has little mechanistic basis to produce major benefit in TNBC outside of rare stochastic immune re-priming events.
Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020.

Mechanistically accurate: Atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1 IgG1; DrugBank DB11595, ChEMBL CHEMBL3707227) blocks PD-L1–PD-1/CD80 and promotes expansion of effector T cells and associated PD-1-axis pathway genes when therapy is effective.
DrugBank Atezolizumab (DB11595).(DrugBank) ChEMBL CHEMBL3707227.(EMBL-EBI) Roche Tecentriq PD-L1 MOA.(Roche)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: On-treatment PD-1-axis gene upregulation with progression reflects partial re-activation of exhausted T cells that is insufficient to overcome alternative immune checkpoints or stromal exclusion.
Benci et al. Cell 2019, PMID: 30683432.(Cell)

Mechanistically accurate: Persistently low or paradoxically decreased PD-1-axis signaling after atezolizumab corresponds to immune-desert TNBC where therapy fails to recruit or maintain effector T cells.
Keenan et al. Nat Med 2019.(Europe PMC)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Following an initial phase of pathway hyperactivation and tumor regression, contraction of PD-1-axis gene expression can occur as antigen burden falls while clinical responses are maintained.
Tumeh et al. Nature 2014. PMID: 24619099 (dynamic PD-1-axis activation; cross-cancer).(Portland Press)

HALLMARK_WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING.description: Wnt ligand–driven β-catenin signaling program implicated in tumor cell state and stromal interactions.
HALLMARK_WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING.interpretation: In breast cancer, Wnt/β-catenin activity is linked to immune exclusion and reduced permissiveness of the tumor microenvironment to effective anti-tumor T-cell infiltration.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Tumor-intrinsic Wnt/β-catenin activation excludes BATF3⁺ dendritic cells, preventing CD8⁺ T-cell priming and creating non-T-cell-inflamed tumors resistant to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade; this immune-excluded program, though best shown in melanoma, is also observed in TNBC subsets.
Spranger et al., “Tumor-resident β-catenin prevents anti-tumour immunity.” Nature 2015. PMID: 26123020 (melanoma; cross-cancer).(MDPI)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Wnt/β-catenin-high TNBC might still respond if parallel pathways (e.g., strong neoantigen load, HRD) overcome dendritic cell exclusion, but such co-occurrence is atypical.
Spranger et al. Nature 2015, PMID: 26123020 (cross-cancer extrapolation).(MDPI)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Low Wnt/β-catenin removes one barrier to T-cell priming; resistance in this setting usually implies other dominant suppressive programs (e.g., TGF-β–rich stroma or IDO1).
Luke et al., JCO 2019 review on Wnt/β-catenin and ICI resistance (cross-cancer).(GSEA MSigDB)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Wnt/β-catenin-low breast tumors are more permissive for BATF3⁺ dendritic-cell recruitment and CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, supporting atezolizumab sensitivity when other inflamed features are present.
Spranger et al. Nature 2015, PMID: 26123020 (mechanism; cross-cancer).(MDPI)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Under ICI pressure, outgrowth of Wnt/β-catenin-high clones can re-establish dendritic-cell exclusion and drive acquired resistance to PD-L1 blockade.
Spranger et al. Nature 2015, PMID: 26123020 (adaptive Wnt-high immune exclusion; cross-cancer).(MDPI)
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Sustained upregulation of Wnt/β-catenin after PD-L1 blockade would be expected to counteract T-cell priming and is inconsistent with durable atezolizumab sensitivity in breast cancer.
Luke et al. JCO 2019 (Wnt/β-catenin & ICI resistance).(GSEA MSigDB)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: If Wnt/β-catenin decreases but tumors remain resistant, other pathways (e.g., TGF-β, hypoxia) must dominantly maintain immune exclusion.
Mariathasan et al. Nature 2018, PMID: 29443960 (TGF-β immune exclusion; cross-cancer).(PubMed)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Combination strategies or clonal selection that reduce Wnt/β-catenin activity can restore dendritic-cell recruitment and intratumoral CD8⁺ T cells, potentiating atezolizumab benefit.
Spranger et al. Nature 2015, PMID: 26123020 (cross-cancer).(MDPI)

HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING.description: TGF-β signaling program regulating fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and immune suppression.
HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING.interpretation: This pathway contributes to immune-excluded tumor states in breast cancer by promoting stromal barriers and immunosuppressive cues that limit effective immune-cell penetration.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High stromal TGF-β signaling defines an immune-excluded phenotype with peritumoral but not intratumoral CD8⁺ T cells and is associated with poor response to atezolizumab in urothelial cancer and immune-excluded TNBC.

Mariathasan et al., “TGFβ attenuates tumour response to PD-L1 blockade by contributing to exclusion of T cells.” Nature 2018. PMID: 29443960 (urothelial, cross-cancer but mechanistically relevant).(PubMed)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: A subset of TGF-β–high TNBC may respond if coexisting features (e.g., very high TMB or strong HRD-driven immunogenicity) partially overcome stromal exclusion, but this is atypical.
Mariathasan et al. Nature 2018, PMID: 29443960 (cross-cancer extrapolation).(PubMed)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Low TGF-β removes one barrier to T-cell infiltration; resistance in this context usually reflects alternative suppressive axes (e.g., Wnt/β-catenin, IDO1).
Mariathasan et al. Nature 2018, PMID: 29443960.(PubMed)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: TGF-β–low TNBC is less likely to exhibit stromal trapping of T cells and more likely to permit intratumoral CD8⁺ infiltration, favoring atezolizumab sensitivity when PD-L1 and TILs are present.
Mariathasan et al. Nature 2018, PMID: 29443960.(PubMed)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: On-treatment upregulation of TGF-β/EMT programs under PD-L1 blockade can maintain immune exclusion and is a hallmark of acquired resistance in immune-excluded breast tumors.
Mariathasan et al. Nature 2018, PMID: 29443960 (combo anti-TGF-β + anti-PD-L1 restores CD8⁺ infiltration).(PubMed)
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Persistent or increasing TGF-β signaling after therapy would be expected to trap T cells in peritumoral stroma and undermine durable atezolizumab benefit.
Mariathasan et al. Nature 2018, PMID: 29443960.(PubMed)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: If TGF-β signaling decreases but tumors still progress, this implies that other dominant mechanisms (e.g., Wnt, hypoxia, or HR restoration) substitute for TGF-β–mediated exclusion.
Clark et al., “Harnessing DNA repair defects to augment immune-based cancer therapy.” Front Oncol 2021. PMID: 34307267 (cross-cancer).
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Decrease in TGF-β signaling, whether by combination therapy or therapy-induced remodeling, correlates with improved CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and synergy with PD-L1 blockade.
Mariathasan et al. Nature 2018, PMID: 29443960.(PubMed)

GOBP_ANTIGEN_PROCESSING_AND_PRESENTATION.description: Processes enabling antigen processing and presentation (including MHC class I presentation) required for T-cell recognition of tumor antigens.
GOBP_ANTIGEN_PROCESSING_AND_PRESENTATION.interpretation: Effective antigen presentation is fundamental to T-cell–mediated killing in breast cancer immunotherapy; defects in this process enable immune escape despite checkpoint blockade.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High expression of MHC-I/II, B2M, TAP, and immunoproteasome genes indicates intact antigen processing/presentation, which supports TIL recruitment and better response to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors in TNBC.

GO:0019882 antigen processing and presentation.(GSEA MSigDB) Silva et al., “Immune checkpoint inhibitors in tumors harboring HRD.” Cancers 2022. PMID: 35267947 (HRD/antigenicity; cross-cancer).(PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with robust antigen presentation, resistance can arise if downstream immune steps fail (e.g., T-cell exclusion via Wnt or TGF-β), but this discordant pattern is uncommon.
Zaretsky et al., “Mutations associated with acquired resistance to PD-1 blockade.” NEJM 2016. PMID: 27433843 (B2M/JAK mutations; cross-cancer).(MGI Mouse Genome Informatics)
Mechanistically accurate: Low expression of HLA/B2M/TAP in breast tumors mirrors antigen-presentation defects linked to primary resistance to ICIs.
Zaretsky et al. NEJM 2016, PMID: 27433843 (B2M loss).(MGI Mouse Genome Informatics)
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Without sufficient baseline antigen presentation, there is no efficient TCR recognition, making robust atezolizumab sensitivity implausible outside rare cases of rapid epigenetic re-expression.
Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790.
Mechanistically accurate: IFN-γ produced by reinvigorated T cells under PD-L1 blockade upregulates HLA/B2M/TAP and immunoproteasome genes, amplifying antigen presentation and atezolizumab efficacy.
Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338.(PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Restoration of antigen presentation with persistent resistance suggests alternative immune escape (e.g., loss of IFN-γ receptor, dominant myeloid/TGF-β suppression).
Zaretsky et al. NEJM 2016, PMID: 27433843.(MGI Mouse Genome Informatics)
Mechanistically accurate: On-treatment selection for B2M or HLA loss-of-function clones abrogates antigen presentation and leads to acquired resistance to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade.
Zaretsky et al. NEJM 2016, PMID: 27433843 (B2M loss under PD-1).(MGI Mouse Genome Informatics)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In principle, effective early responses could eliminate highly antigenic clones, leaving residual low-presentation cells while the patient remains clinically responsive, but this is an uncommon and unstable state.
Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790.

GOBP_REGULATION_OF_T_CELL_ACTIVATION.description: Biological processes that regulate T-cell activation states through cytokines, antigen presentation, and receptor–ligand interactions.
GOBP_REGULATION_OF_T_CELL_ACTIVATION.interpretation: T-cell activation programs shape whether breast tumors are immune-inflamed versus immune suppressed, influencing the capacity of checkpoint blockade to restore cytotoxic function.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Upregulation of genes regulating T-cell activation (GO:0050863; costimulatory receptors, cytokines) in TNBC correlates with high TILs and better outcomes with checkpoint blockade.
GO BP: regulation of T-cell activation (GO:0050863).(GSEA MSigDB) Dixon-Douglas et al., “Integrating immunotherapy into the treatment landscape of TNBC.” ASCO Ed Book 2022.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some breast tumors show high expression of activation regulators but dominance of negative regulators (e.g., CTLA-4, PD-1, LAG3), leading to exhausted T cells and resistance.
Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790.
Mechanistically accurate: Low expression of genes regulating T-cell activation indicates poor priming and anergic or absent T cells, a typical profile of cold TNBC poorly responsive to atezolizumab.
De Santis et al., “Early-stage TNBC: current landscape.” Exploration Targeted Anti-Tumor Therapy 2024.
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Without transcriptional evidence of T-cell activation, PD-L1 blockade has no substantial T-cell population to re-engage, making true sensitivity highly unlikely.
Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338.(PubMed)
Mechanistically accurate: Responders typically show on-treatment upregulation of activation-related genes (CD27, IFNG, GZMB) indicating successful T-cell priming and expansion under PD-L1 blockade.
Ayers et al. JCI 2017, PMID: 28650338; “T cell–inflamed GEP.”(PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Persistent expression of activation markers with no tumor shrinkage suggests ineffective or misdirected activation (e.g., Treg or non-tumor-specific T-cell expansion).
Benci et al. Cell 2019, PMID: 30683432 (adaptive resistance; cross-cancer).(Cell)
Mechanistically accurate: Failure to induce or sustain T-cell activation genes under atezolizumab indicates lack of immune engagement and matches non-responder transcriptional profiles.
Keenan et al. Nat Med 2019.(Europe PMC)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: After a strong but transient activation wave and tumor clearance, late samples can show reduced activation signatures while clinical benefit persists.
Tumeh et al. Nature 2014. PMID: 24619099.(Portland Press)

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Oncogenic PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling program controlling cell survival, growth, metabolism, and microenvironmental signaling.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: In breast cancer, PI3K/AKT/mTOR activity is described as contributing to an immune-suppressive milieu and reduced tumor immune infiltration, impacting responsiveness to PD-L1 blockade.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Tumor-intrinsic PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation (e.g., PTEN loss, PIK3CA mutations) promotes PD-L1 expression, reduces MHC, and fosters immunosuppressive cytokines, contributing to ICI resistance in breast cancer.

Pan-cancer PD-L1 regulation by AKT–mTOR: “Control of PD-L1 expression by oncogenic activation of the AKT–mTOR pathway.” Cancer Res 2016. PMID: 26677869. Prabhu et al., PI3K/AKT/mTOR in breast cancer. Naunyn Schmiedebergs Arch Pharmacol 2025.
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Highly proliferative PI3K-activated TNBC may still respond if immunogenic (e.g., HRD, high TMB) and heavily infiltrated by T cells, but oncogenic PI3K generally biases toward immune escape.
Silva et al. Cancers 2022 (HRD, PD-L1, ICI).(PubMed)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Low PI3K signaling removes a major oncogenic immune-evasion driver; resistance in this setting usually reflects independent suppressive pathways (e.g., TGF-β, Wnt, IDO1).
Quan et al., “Clinical implications of the interaction between PD-1/PD-L1 and PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway.” J Cancer 2022. PMID: 35370918 (NSCLC; cross-cancer).
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: PI3K-low tumors lack this specific PD-L1-inducing immune-escape axis, so if other inflamed features are present, they are more permissive to atezolizumab response.
Prabhu et al. 2025 review PI3K/AKT/mTOR in breast cancer.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: On-treatment hyperactivation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR can upregulate PD-L1 and survival signaling, enabling tumor immune escape and acquired resistance to PD-L1 blockade.
Pan et al., “Control of PD-L1 expression by oncogenic activation of the AKT–mTOR pathway.” Cancer Res 2016. PMID: 26677869.
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Sustained PI3K/AKT/mTOR upregulation underlies immune evasion and counters the benefits of PD-L1 blockade, so true durable sensitivity with rising PI3K signaling is biologically inconsistent.
Quan et al. J Cancer 2022, PMID: 35370918.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: If PI3K signaling decreases (e.g., via combination with PI3K inhibitors) but resistance persists, other adaptive pathways (e.g., JAK/STAT defects, antigen-presentation loss) likely predominate.
Garg et al., “Strategic advancements in targeting PI3K/AKT/mTOR in cancer.” Biochem Pharmacol 2025.(Nature)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Dual reduction in oncogenic PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling and PD-L1-mediated immune evasion (e.g., via combination regimens) enhances T-cell function and supports atezolizumab sensitivity.
Quan et al. J Cancer 2022, PMID: 35370918 (rationale for combining ICIs with PI3K pathway inhibitors).

HALLMARK_HYPOXIA.description: Hypoxia-response transcriptional program driven by low oxygen stress and associated microenvironmental remodeling.
HALLMARK_HYPOXIA.interpretation: Hypoxia-related programs in breast cancer are associated with immune dysfunction and reduced immune-cell infiltration, shaping an environment less favorable for effective checkpoint inhibitor activity.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Hypoxia/HIF-1α upregulates PD-L1 and VEGF, recruits MDSCs, and impairs T- and NK-cell function, correlating with poor ICI responses in multiple tumors including TNBC.
Chen et al., “Hypoxic microenvironment in cancer.” Sig Transduct Target Ther 2023. PMID: 36859563.(Cell) Khan et al., “Hypoxia: syndicating TNBC against modern therapeutics.” Front Oncol 2023.
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: While hypoxia can increase PD-L1 expression (creating a target for atezolizumab), the net effect is typically immunosuppressive; sensitivity in strongly hypoxic TNBC is unusual without vascular/anti-VEGF modulation.
Bailey et al., “Targeting HIF-1α abrogates PD-L1–mediated immune escape.” Cancer Immunol Res 2022. PMID: 35338055 (cross-cancer).

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Normoxic tumors lacking hypoxic suppression but still resistant to atezolizumab must harbor other dominant immune-evasion pathways.
Chen et al. 2023 review, PMID: 36859563.(Cell)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low hypoxia/HIF-1α signaling reduces PD-L1 induction and immunosuppressive metabolites, favoring T-cell function and atezolizumab sensitivity in inflamed TNBC.
Obeagu et al., “Hypoxia-inducible factors in breast cancer: prognostic implications.” Ann Med Surg 2025.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistent or increased hypoxia under treatment sustains HIF-1α–mediated PD-L1 and VEGF, supporting treatment resistance despite PD-L1 blockade.
Chen et al. 2023, PMID: 36859563; Musleh Ud Din et al., hypoxia and immune escape. Int J Mol Sci 2024.(Cell)
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Increased hypoxia/HIF-1α post-therapy would be expected to enhance PD-L1 and immunosuppression, opposing durable atezolizumab benefit in breast cancer.
Bailey et al. Cancer Immunol Res 2022, PMID: 35338055.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: If hypoxia lessens yet tumors progress, non-hypoxia-mediated escape (e.g., antigen loss or Wnt activation) must maintain resistance.
Clark et al. Front Oncol 2021, PMID: 34307267 (DNA repair & immune; cross-cancer).
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Tumor debulking and vascular remodeling can reduce hypoxia and HIF-1α-driven PD-L1, improving effector T-cell function and consolidating atezolizumab responses.
Chen et al. 2023, PMID: 36859563; Khan et al. 2023 TNBC hypoxia review.(Cell)

KEGG_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBINATION.description: Homologous recombination DNA double-strand break repair pathway (HR) that maintains genome integrity.
KEGG_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBINATION.interpretation: In breast cancer, homologous recombination deficiency is discussed as increasing genomic instability and tumor immunogenicity, providing context for immune engagement relevant to checkpoint inhibitor response.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High expression of HR genes (BRCA1/2, RAD51; KEGG hsa03440) indicates HR-proficient tumors with lower mutational/neoantigen burden, which are generally less immunogenic and less likely to benefit from PD-L1 blockade.
KEGG Homologous recombination – Homo sapiens (hsa03440).(Genome 日本) Pellegrino et al., “HRR deficiency and ICI efficacy.” Clin Lung Cancer 2020. PMID: 32035827 (cross-cancer).(Europe PMC)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: There are HR-proficient TNBCs with high TILs and PD-L1 where atezolizumab can still work, but HR proficiency itself does not drive sensitivity and may even oppose it.
Telli et al., “HRD across TNBC subtypes and host immunity.” Breast Cancer Res 2018. PMID: 29301592.

Mechanistically accurate: HRD/BRCA1/2-mutated TNBC exhibits genomic instability, higher TMB, more TILs and PD-L1 expression, providing a mechanistic basis for enhanced sensitivity to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade.
Silva et al. Cancers 2022. PMID: 35267947.(PubMed) Yndestad et al., “HRD and TILs/PD-L1 across breast cancer.” Genes 2024. PMID: 38200807.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: HRD with resistance to atezolizumab suggests that suppressive microenvironmental programs (e.g., TGF-β, Wnt, IDO1) can override HRD-driven immunogenicity.
Clark et al. Front Oncol 2021, PMID: 34307267 (HRD + immune escape).
Mechanistically accurate: Acquired restoration of HR (e.g., BRCA reversion) can reduce neoantigen generation and support immune escape, contributing to late resistance to ICI-containing regimens.
Ali et al., “Genomic features of HRD across breast cancer.” Genes 2024. PMID: 38377965.
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Sustained or increased HR capacity would usually diminish immunogenicity; any residual sensitivity likely reflects immune memory generated earlier in an HRD phase.
Telli et al. Breast Cancer Res 2018, PMID: 29301592 (cross-cancer reasoning).

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Persistent HRD after therapy but progression suggests that immune editing or TME-mediated suppression (e.g., Tregs, MDSCs) outweigh HRD-related immunogenicity.
Clark et al. Front Oncol 2021, PMID: 34307267.
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Continued HRD maintains neoantigen generation and, combined with sustained immune engagement under PD-L1 blockade, supports durable responses or synergy with DNA-damaging chemotherapy in TNBC.
Yndestad et al. Genes 2024, PMID: 38200807. De La Cruz et al., TNBC immune markers and prognosis.

GOBP_KYNURENINE_METABOLIC_PROCESS.description: Tryptophan catabolism to kynurenine and related metabolites, a metabolic axis that can modulate immune responses.
GOBP_KYNURENINE_METABOLIC_PROCESS.interpretation: Kynurenine-pathway activity is described as creating a metabolically immunosuppressive environment that can dampen anti-tumor T-cell function in breast cancer.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Upregulated tryptophan–kynurenine metabolism (IDO1/TDO2) activates AhR in T cells and promotes Treg and MDSC expansion, which suppress effector immunity and mediate resistance to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors; this axis is active in TNBC.
GO:0070189 kynurenine metabolic process.(GSEA MSigDB) Zhai et al., IDO1–kynurenine–AhR immune suppression (cross-cancer).(ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Even though IFN-γ in responders can induce IDO1, pre-existing high kynurenine pathway activity usually signals strong immunosuppression and poor response, with sensitivity only possible if other pro-immune features dominate.
Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790.
Mechanistically accurate: Low kynurenine metabolism reduces Treg induction and allows more effective CD8⁺ responses under PD-L1 blockade in breast tumors.
Zhai et al. IDO1/AhR review (cross-cancer).(ScienceDirect)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Resistance despite low kynurenine signaling implies that other inhibitory circuits (e.g., TGF-β, Wnt, HR restoration) dominate the tumor–immune interface.
Clark et al. Front Oncol 2021, PMID: 34307267.
Mechanistically accurate: IFN-γ released after PD-L1 blockade can paradoxically induce IDO1/TDO2 and kynurenine, creating an adaptive resistance loop that dampens T-cell responses.
Benci et al. Cell 2019, PMID: 30683432 (adaptive resistance; cross-cancer).(Cell)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Any increase in kynurenine metabolism in responders would usually be transient and counterbalanced by strong effector T-cell expansion or concomitant IDO1 inhibition.
Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Reduced kynurenine signaling but continued resistance suggests alternative acquired escape such as antigen loss or stromal exclusion.
Clark et al. Front Oncol 2021, PMID: 34307267.
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Successful responses may be accompanied by reduced IDO1/TDO2 expression and lower kynurenine, as immunosuppressive feedback loops are disrupted and tumor burden decreases.
Zhai et al. (IDO1/AhR; cross-cancer).(ScienceDirect)

GOBP_REGULATION_OF_T_CELL_COSTIMULATION.description: Processes regulating co-stimulatory signaling necessary for full T-cell activation (e.g., CD28/B7 and cytokine support).
GOBP_REGULATION_OF_T_CELL_COSTIMULATION.interpretation: Adequate co-stimulation is necessary for effective T-cell activation; deficits in co-stimulatory signaling can limit the effectiveness of checkpoint blockade in breast tumors.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High expression of genes regulating T-cell costimulation (CD28/B7 family, TNFR superfamily; GO:2000523) reflects robust antigen-presenting cell–T-cell interactions that favor strong responses to PD-L1 blockade in TNBC.
GO BP: regulation of T-cell costimulation (GO:2000523).(GSEA MSigDB) Ayers et al. JCI 2017, costimulatory genes in T cell–inflamed GEP. PMID: 28650338.(PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Costimulatory regulation can be skewed toward inhibitory ligands or dysfunctional APC–T-cell contacts, so a minority of tumors with high costimulation-related transcripts still fail PD-L1 blockade.
Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790.
Mechanistically accurate: Low costimulation signaling means T cells cannot be effectively primed, limiting the impact of PD-L1 blockade even when PD-L1 is expressed in TNBC.
De Santis et al. 2024 TNBC review.
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Without costimulatory support, TCR signals remain weak and PD-L1 blockade alone cannot fully activate cytotoxic responses in breast cancer.
Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790.
Mechanistically accurate: Effective atezolizumab can enhance costimulatory circuits (e.g., CD28–CD80/86, CD27, 4-1BB) by relieving PD-L1-mediated inhibition, promoting full T-cell activation.
Ayers et al. JCI 2017 (CD27, costimulatory genes in responder signatures). PMID: 28650338.(PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: If costimulation genes rise but tumors still progress, this suggests co-dominant inhibitory receptors (TIM-3, TIGIT, LAG3) or physical exclusion blocking effective tumor killing.
Benci et al. Cell 2019, PMID: 30683432.(Cell)
Mechanistically accurate: Failure to sustain costimulatory signaling under therapy indicates T-cell anergy or deletion, consistent with non-response or early relapse after atezolizumab.
Han et al. Cancer Treat Rev 2020, PMID: 32004790.
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: After effective tumor clearance, overall immune activation and costimulatory tone can contract while clinical responses persist due to immune memory and minimal residual disease.
Tumeh et al. Nature 2014, PMID: 24619099 (dynamic T-cell responses under PD-1 blockade; cross-cancer).(Portland Press)

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: PD-L1 (CD274) expression is described as required for atezolizumab to have a target in breast cancer, and PD-L1–positive TNBC showed benefit in IMpassion130.
CXCL9 is listed among IFN-γ–responsive genes associated with a T-cell–inflamed tumor state that supports immune-cell recruitment in responding tumors.
CXCL10 is listed among IFN-γ–responsive genes associated with chemokine-driven lymphocyte trafficking in immune-inflamed breast tumors.
CCL5 is described as a chemokine whose upregulation is associated with recruitment of immune cells into the tumor microenvironment in sensitivity contexts.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: BRCA1/2-mutated or HRD-high TNBC is described as more immunogenic (higher mutation load/neoantigens and TIL-rich, PD-L1–positive environment), consistent with improved responsiveness to checkpoint blockade in the subtype discussion.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Compensatory upregulation of alternative immune checkpoints such as LAG-3 is described as a resistance mechanism after PD-1/PD-L1 axis blockade.
TIM-3 (HAVCR2) is described as another checkpoint that can be upregulated in TNBC following PD-1/PD-L1 blockade, contributing to continued T-cell dysfunction.
CTLA-4 is mentioned as an additional inhibitory pathway that could contribute to residual immune suppression when upregulated.
IDO1 is described as an immunosuppressive enzyme that increases kynurenine and suppresses T-cell proliferation, contributing to resistance under immune pressure.
IL-10 is described as an anti-inflammatory cytokine that can dampen immune responses even when PD-L1 is blocked.
VEGF-A is described as promoting angiogenesis and inhibiting immune-cell trafficking/function, correlating with poorer immunotherapy response.
Hypoxia programs (linked to HIF-1α activity) are described as associated with immune exclusion and resistance to checkpoint blockade in breast cancer.
MYC overexpression is described as fostering immune evasion, including suppression of immune responses and reduced efficacy of checkpoint blockade unless MYC-driven processes are addressed.
FOXP3+ regulatory T-cell enrichment is described as part of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that reduces atezolizumab efficacy.
ARG1 is listed among myeloid-derived suppressor cell–associated pathways that promote suppressive immune infiltrates and reduce checkpoint inhibitor efficacy.
IL-6 is listed among pathways supporting immunosuppressive myeloid programs (MDSC-associated), contributing to resistance contexts.
CCR4 is referenced as a factor involved in Treg recruitment; higher Treg-associated pathways are described as reducing immunotherapy efficacy.
CXCR2 is described in the context of myeloid/neutrophil (MDSC) recruitment pathways that can suppress effector T-cell activity and reduce checkpoint inhibitor response.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss of antigen presentation via B2M disruption is described as allowing tumors to evade T-cell recognition despite checkpoint blockade.
A JAK1 truncating mutation is described in a non-responding TNBC case, consistent with loss of interferon signaling and reduced immune-mediated tumor killing.
Loss of JAK1/2-mediated interferon signaling is described as a resistance route by preventing interferon-driven antigen presentation and related immune responses.
PTEN loss (with increased PI3K pathway signaling) is described as being linked to an immune-cold microenvironment and poorer response to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade.
Loss of antigen-processing machinery components such as TAP transporters is described as an example of antigen presentation pathway downregulation that can drive immune escape.

PD-L1–negative tumors are described as having no target for atezolizumab and did not benefit in the PD-L1–negative TNBC subgroup discussion, consistent with resistance when CD274 is low/absent.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC): This is the only subtype with proven clinical benefit from atezolizumab; IMpassion130 showed PD-L1–positive TNBC derived PFS benefit, with PD-L1 positivity on immune cells (≥1% IC by SP142 assay) required for efficacy.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Basal-like immune-activated (BLIA) TNBC: Responded best; characterized by high TILs, PD-L1, and low EMT/stroma.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Basal-like immune-suppressed (BLIS) TNBC: Responded poorly; characterized by high TGF-β and low immune infiltration, with immunosuppressive stroma and immune exclusion.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal) Breast Cancer: Generally low PD-L1 expression and low TIL levels; trials have shown very low response rates and atezolizumab is not indicated for HR+ disease outside rare clinical trial anecdotes.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Positive Breast Cancer: Combination immunotherapy strategies are investigational; KATE2 (T-DM1 ± atezolizumab) did not meet the primary PFS endpoint overall, with a numerical PFS improvement in the PD-L1+ subgroup reported as small-sample exploratory.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA-Mutated/HRD+ Cancers: A significant fraction of TNBC (and some luminal B) tumors have HRD; BRCA/HRD+ status is described as suggestive of an inflamed tumor microenvironment due to more neoantigens, potentially contributing to atezolizumab efficacy, though not all HRD+ tumors have TILs.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.PD-L1–Negative TNBC: Did not benefit in IMpassion130; described as an immune-cold subset often with low TILs and may require additional interventions to induce inflammation.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Tumor Mutational Burden (TMB) High Subse: A minority of breast tumors have very high TMB; such tumors may respond better to PD-1/L1 inhibitors, but this is described as not specifically studied for atezolizumab in breast cancer and remains a rare subset.
